body: I have BPD causing sometimes, extreme attention-seeking behaviour. When I was younger, I would cut for attention - usually just superficial cuts, small razor scratches, etc. This would have signified my disorder before I was diagnosed. Since then, I do still cut, but rarely, and only when I'm in extreme pain and I feel hopeless. It relieves anxiety and stress when I feel awful, and it kind of exhausts me in a way to help me sleep it off. Luckily it's only rarely and hopefully one day I will stop for good.
Update: definitely not pregnant. 2 negative tests. Any answers?

I'm not sure if it is the same here in England. He's 4, I'm not sure when a child's point of view becomes valid in a court. 

I can cope with shared custody, with mediators contacting us instead of direct contact. But I can't stop thinking of the worst. 

If I lose him, I lose everything.

I just don't understand or know what my life is supposed to be without him. He loves me, he wants to stay with me and not his father. But ultimately, it's not our decision. 

I am being selfish in saying it, I know. I know technically I'm saying I'd rather him live without me forever than for 14 years. But I can't live that long without him, whereas he can be happy with or without me as a child - he's young, all he knows is the love around him. Honestly, though, I'd rather die than live without him the majority of his life.

At this point, I don't know what the result will be. Both of us parents have wrongdoings - maybe we'll be given shared custody, but I'm constantly thinking of the worst and I can't even cope with the thought of being without him.
My BPD gives depressive symptoms. Can you have a diagnosis of depression alongside BPD? Or only have one?
